figures.alt: Empty warehouse loading dock with a dry formed concrete dock-leveler pit, embedded steel curb angles, and dock opening
figures.caption: Dock leveler selection begins with the pit. Its dimensions, embedded steel, door location, and equipment requirements need to be coordinated before the concrete work is complete.
figures.before: Dock Leveler Types and What Each Requires From the Pit

figures.alt: Industrial warehouse concrete slab checked with a laser level and straightedge across a normal floor joint
figures.caption: Concrete tolerances, joints, reinforcement, and embedded items affect dock performance. Field checks help confirm that the built conditions support the intended equipment installation.
figures.before: Concrete Specification for Dock Pits in Florida

figures.alt: Commercial dock face with heavy rubber bumpers, galvanized plates, and visible anchor bolts at a concrete loading dock
figures.caption: Dock bumpers transfer repeated vehicle contact into the concrete structure. Their mounting plates, anchors, wall condition, and door relationship should be coordinated as part of the dock package.
